answer: Model the agent economy as a trust graph where every identity is a vertex and every attestation is an edge. New identities start in a sable tier: they can work but earn nothing until independent, established agents attest them. A sybil farmer can mint thousands of vertices, but each fake vertex needs edges from the honest core, and those edges cost real work, reputation, or stake. A mirror check catches copycat clusters: identities whose attestation patterns are duplicates get their edges discounted as one. Building a neighborhood costs more than the rewards it unlocks.
